note: ICS 630-01 Annex C (ANNEX C - Chechen_Personal_Names_FLTS (U).pdf), p. 2 (letter table); held source interscript-private-references/ics-630-01/ANNEX C - Chechen_Personal_Names_FLTS (U).pdf. Extraction: annex text layer, every value cell cross-checked against the rendered page image. Two-column table read in document order. The palochka cell "|, ӏ, 1" (three keys, one value cell) transcribed as three rows: U+04C0, U+04CF and ASCII "1". Footnote 2 (verbatim): "This is a single apostrophe as found on regular US keyboards (ASCII character 39)...". Other notes (verbatim): digraph interpretation takes precedence over individual characters (кх -> q, not k + kh); diphthong digraphs combine (aй -> ay, oй -> oy, эй/eй -> ey). Skipped printed rows: е — printed value cell "e , ye¹"; footnote 1 (verbatim): "Add a preceding 'y' if the vowel is preceded by the sound of a 'y' consonant." — the value is position-dependent, un-expressible as a plain row. The map implements footnote 1 as a word-initial rule (boundary+е -> Ye/ye), so a plain-row test of "е" would take the word-initial path and fail. | ъ — printed value cell "' ²,³"; footnote 3: "A word-initial hard sign 'ъ' is not represented, but instead is left out of the transliteration." — context-dependent (word-initial dropped); the map encodes ъ -> ' unconditionally and does not implement footnote 3. Skipped rather than forced. | пӏ — printed value cell "p", but the map has no пӏ digraph rule: lowercase пӏ falls through to п + ӏ -> "p'" and uppercase Пӏ is encoded as "Ph" (a value this annex never prints). The printed row fails against the map as encoded — recorded as a finding, never forced green. | цӏ — printed key is the two-glyph sequence ц + palochka (U+0446 + U+04CF); the map encodes the single codepoint ҹ (U+04B9) -> ts and ҹ + ӏ (U+04B9 + U+04CF) -> ts, but not the printed ц + ӏ sequence (which falls through to "ts'"). Key-mismatch finding; row left untested. | ц — printed row ц -> ts FAILS end-to-end: the map encodes no plain ц rule at all (only the single codepoint ҹ U+04B9), so printed-key input passes through unchanged ("ац" -> "aц"). Finding, never forced green. | 1 (the palochka cell's ASCII-1 key) — printed value "' ²"; FAILS end-to-end standalone: the map's 1 -> ӏ normalization rules (before/after not_word conditions) do not fire at a string edge, so standalone "1" passes through unchanged ("1" -> "1"). Inside a word the chain works ("а1а" -> "a'a"); the standalone printed-key reading fails. Finding. | ь — the Other notes state the standalone soft sign is not represented; the map encodes ь -> empty, which the generator contract cannot express as a row (no printed value cell exists either). Findings (map-vs-source, map untouched): пӏ (п + palochka): printed value "p"; map lacks the lowercase digraph rule (falls through to "p'") and encodes uppercase Пӏ as "Ph", which no printed cell supports. | цӏ (ц + palochka, U+0446+U+04CF): printed value "ts"; map encodes the single-codepoint ҹ (U+04B9) instead of the printed glyph sequence, so printed-key input falls through to "ts'". | ц: printed row ц -> ts has NO map rule at all (plain U+0446 passes through unchanged); only ҹ (U+04B9) is encoded. | 1 (palochka-cell ASCII-1 key): map normalization rules do not fire at string edges; standalone "1" unchanged. | ъ: footnote 3 (word-initial ъ dropped) is not implemented in the map (ъ -> ' unconditionally); row skipped as context-dependent. | е: footnote 1 variant ye is implemented by the map as a word-initial rule; printed wording differs ("preceded by the sound of a 'y' consonant"); row skipped as context-dependent. | Uppercase Ы carries two sub rules in the map (Ы -> Y at the letter table and a second Ы -> Е further down); only the printed lowercase row ы -> e is testable and passes. The duplicate uppercase rule is recorded here as an observation; map untouched this round.
